snippet.title: SOMA native VR mod - Trailer
snippet.description:
It's time to return to PATHOS-II... In VR.

DISCORD.GG/FLAT2VR

---------------------------------------------------------------

What changed since my last video:

- All Omni-Tool upgrades are now manual. You'd physically grab the Tool Chip, Cortex Chip, etc, and place them on the Omni-Tool to install it.

- All key items now have manual interactions in terms of usage and acquisiton. This includes Structure gel, Energy Pal, ENV chip, Scan Chip, Simulation Asset Device, Tool Chips, and Cortex Chips, etc.

- Shoulder stowing - you can now stow and retrieve key items from your left shoulder. I've also moved the Omni-Tool right hip holster to your right shoulder, so you'd reach over your right shoulder to stow or retrieve your Omni-Tool.

- Haptics - your controller, left or right, depending on which hand is performing the action, will now emit a pulse when you're able to interact with something, and when interacting with things, like drawers, doors, items, grabbing loose objects, using the scanner, special interactions, like interacting with robots, climbing into vents, etc. This should make it easier for players to know when they're able to interact with things.

- Physical interactions with terminals. The cursor is gone in terminals. You'd have to use your fingers to tap on the screen to navigate, or drag your fingers across the screen for special interactions, just like using a smartphone.

- All readables/interactables, like documents, pictures, notepads, notes, etc, are now physically interactable. You can grab them with your hands, rotate, and throw them.

- Added another option in the pause menu and main menu - "VR SETTINGS". This is to control comfort settings and holsters. More options may be introduced in the future. The VR SETTINGS menu was created to match SOMA's native GUI aesthetics, font, and navigation to look like a native menu option. You'll have the option to enable smooth turning, Snap turning (30-45 degrees),  HMD movement, body movement, the option to disable some image distortions that may induce nausea, increase/decrease distance for subtitles, world scale, and more. Additionally, VR users with VR headsets with eye-tracking can now use SOMA's special eye-tracking features, as showcased in Frictional Games's "Tobii Eye Tracking" SOMA video.

- Hand model improvements - SOMA's lighting and shadows will now affect the hand models, instead of constantly looking bright.

- Added support for full-finger tracking [EXPERIMENTAL/UNTESTED, CAN'T TEST AS I DON'T HAVE ANY CONTROLLERS THAT SUPPORT FULL-FINGER TRACKING]

- Added support for vive trackers and natural locomotion for hip-based tracking [EXPERIMENTAL/UNTESTED]

- Manual healing added. Shove your fist in the WAU flower to heal. For earlier interactions, you'd have to grab the WAU flower, until you reach Lambda.

- Added manual interactions for plugs and sockets [for instance, restoring power to the DUNBAT control board using the cable].

- Added a new gesture - press grip or trigger on your head to turn your flashlight on/off.

- Fixed some issues with the manual Omni-Tool interactions.

- Fixed some issues with manual key-item interactions.

- Fixed some issues with hinged doors, levers, wheels, etc.

- Fixed some crashing issues in certain areas.

- Fixed issues regarding multi-body object grabbing and manipulation.
